name: CA-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 26 points on the partisan index
Incumbent Mullin has raised about $970,000 while challenger Hoelter shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a near-certain Democratic hold at roughly 96 percent
No public polling; the margin estimate rests on district fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 26-point Democratic lean, Mullin's roughly $970,000 in fundraising against a challenger with no money on file, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the incumbent's structural edge reinforced by negligible outside spending on either side.
model.watch: A late scandal, a sudden infusion of outside spending against Mullin, or an unexpectedly active challenger campaign could tighten the margin, though an outright upset would be a major surprise.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 15th District leans Democratic by roughly 26 points, one of the stronger Democratic tilts among House seats. Kevin Mullin, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term and has raised about $970,000, while Republican Charles Hoelter shows no fundraising on file and little visible campaign activity. Mullin advanced through the top-two primary, and outside spending in the race is negligible.

No public polls cover the general election, and no expert raters have flagged the seat as competitive. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance near 96 percent. With the incumbent's financial edge and the district's partisan makeup, Democrats are strong favorites to hold the seat; the realistic uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than which party wins.
